title: Push a coolant hose onto a barbed pump outlet and tighten its worm-drive clamp with a nut driver
instruction: Connect the hose to the pump's outlet and clamp it.
context: Fitting a hose to a barbed spigot and clamping it is routine work for auto mechanics and general maintenance and repair workers (coolant, fuel, air and water lines). The hose has to be pushed past the barb's bead all the way to the shoulder, or it blows off under pressure, with the worm-drive clamp's band on the barb behind the bead, and the clamp driven tight with a nut driver: turned, let go and re-gripped as a hand does, while the socket stays seated on the small screw head.
setup: Bench top is z = 0. Coolant pump (painted steel casting 110 x 100 x 110 mm centred at x 0.28, y 0.085 m, on a 150 x 130 x 12 mm base centred at y 0.095; motor housing 80 mm dia, 50 mm long, behind it) bolted down. Its outlet boss (26 mm dia, front face at y 0.025) faces -y and carries a brass hose barb 34 mm long: 11.2 mm shank, 13.6 mm bead 10 mm from its tapered tip; axis 60 mm above the bench at x 0.27. Rubber hose, 12.2 mm bore, 19 mm OD, 200 mm long, 55 g, lying along y with its open end at x 0.27, y -0.12, facing the barb, with a white mark painted 34 mm from that end. On it, band centre 12 mm from the end, a stainless worm-drive clamp (9 mm band, 8 g) run down by hand till it just touches the hose, its screw housing on the arm side (-x), 8 mm hex screw head up. Nut driver: 8 mm socket (14 mm OD, 16 mm long, 9 mm deep), 20 mm shaft, 30 x 30 x 48 mm square grip, 90 g, standing socket-down in a 40 mm square holder at x 0.20, y 0.20.
scoring: 0.25: the hose pushed over the barb's bead (at least 12 mm on). 0.5: pushed fully home, its end within 3 mm of the outlet boss (the white mark then level with the barb's tip). 0.75: also the clamp's band wholly on the barb behind the bead (band centre 6.5 to 17.5 mm from the hose end) and the screw run down snug (real trial: the band no longer turns on the hose by hand). 1.0: also tight (real trial: 3 N m on a torque screwdriver), the driver off the screw, both hands 6 cm clear, held 1 s. Snugging the clamp off the barb or on a hose not home caps the score at 0.5.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The hose is a rigid tube; the bead is drawn only, the barb's collider a slimmer pin. Pushed on lined up, the hose grips the barb by a slide joint (holding it on the barb's axis) with ~3 N drag, sprung against coming off once home. The clamp is held on the hose by a stiff joint. Screw turns come from the seated socket's measured twist: 0.4 turn snug, 0.8 tight, about three half-turns of the wrist; no reaction torque on the driver.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 795 steps.
